correctness.rationale: Four-letter substitution sigma(A)=AB, sigma(B)=CB, sigma(C)=BD, sigma(D)=DD with coding A/B to 1 and C/D to 0 yields recurrences of the binary-digit Baum--Sweet definition. At every level, D_k is zero and A_k=B_k+C_k coordinatewise; therefore each aligned block is coordinatewise bounded by A_k. Each length-2^k shifted window is a suffix and prefix of adjacent aligned blocks and is dominated by a cyclic rotation of A_k, proving the sharp maximum. Block weights satisfy Fibonacci recursion with initial 1,2; arbitrarily long D blocks and one-step window changes give complete interval spectra. Monotonicity sandwiches all n between dyadic scales to prove growth. An independently written digit-word/window enumeration checked dyadic maxima through k=12 and complete spectra through k=9, but the all-n proof is symbolic.

An explicit infinitely long dyadic spectrum and global noninteger exponent answer a substantive structure question, not a rediscovery of the Fibonacci one-count of prefixes.

final_claim: For the Baum--Sweet binary word b(0)=1, every length 2^k factor has at most F_(k+2) ones, attained by the initial prefix; psi_b(2^k)=F_(k+2)+1, and globally psi_b(n)=Theta(n^(log_2 phi)) with the exact exponent in the log limit.
limitations: Dyadic exact count only, global Theta and exponent all lengths, convention b(0)=1 essential.
